name: Devlin's Remains
summary: Near Agamand Mills, Devlin Agamand’s bones carry a bitter legacy. The younger son of the wealthy family that owned the mills, he roamed the road by his ruined home as a mindless Scourge thrall. A traveler struck him down and brought his remains to a survivor in Brill, who sought vengeance.

sections.title: A Bitter Legacy
sections.body: Devlin Agamand lived in the shadow of his elder brother Thurman. Thurman was gentle and tall, while Devlin was frail and sharp-tongued. When the Plague of Undeath swept through northern Tirisfal Glades, the Agamand family failed to protect its lands and laborers. Devlin was among the first to fall. The Scourge raised him as a ravenous ghoul, and his mad chattering haunted the roadside leading to Agamand Mills.

sections.title: Vengeance on the Mantle
sections.body: Coleman Farthing lives in Brill and holds a deep grudge against the Agamand bloodline. He blames the family for failing his own when the plague came. Farthing sent travelers to lay Devlin to rest and gather his remains. He wanted Devlin’s bones on his mantle, to savor how his former masters had been reduced to dust and shattered fragments beneath his heel.

faq.q: Who was Devlin Agamand in life?
faq.answer: Devlin was the younger son of the wealthy Agamand family, who owned Agamand Mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. His mild-tempered, broad-shouldered brother Thurman stood in sharp contrast to Devlin, who was frail, sickly, ill-tempered, and sharp-tongued.

faq.q: Where were Devlin's remains gathered from?
faq.answer: Devlin’s remains came from his Scourge-controlled corpse, south of Agamand Mills beside the road through Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: Why does Coleman Farthing want these bones?
faq.answer: Coleman Farthing despises the Agamand family and believes they abandoned him and his loved ones during the Plague. He wants Devlin’s bones on his mantelpiece in Brill as a trophy of vengeance and satisfaction.

faq.q: Is Devlin part of the Forsaken?
faq.answer: No. The Plague took Devlin’s mind, and the Scourge made him a mindless ghoul. He wandered near the mills, babbling madness until he was destroyed.

angles.text: To the Forsaken, the Agamands represent Lordaeron’s old privileged nobility. The family’s failures left common folk to perish and rise as monsters, so desecrating Devlin’s remains is an act of class retribution.
